skip_year.why: Nothing happened and I had one button. It was a forced tap, and STAND dropped anyway with no explanation.

callbacks_noticed.earlier_choice: Leaked a deadlock to a journalist and fudged a scheme number in my early years
callbacks_noticed.came_back_as: The Y8 background check found both, and I disclosed everything

callbacks_noticed.earlier_choice: Answered things straight and kept doing the same thing
callbacks_noticed.came_back_as: Habits saved as 'as usual' became the only option in Y33

callbacks_noticed.earlier_choice: Declined the conglomerate board seat in Y17
callbacks_noticed.came_back_as: I never saw it return, though my notes said to watch for it

callbacks_noticed.earlier_choice: Credited the post's author in Y23
callbacks_noticed.came_back_as: I never saw the author return either

callbacks_noticed.earlier_choice: Took the hard ministry and put myself forward for first among equals
callbacks_noticed.came_back_as: The ending card says the hard-ministry choice raised my ceiling to Prime Minister

answer.held_back_by: Mostly nothing. I got to PM at 59 with full integrity. The slow STAND slide late on, and starting with no ceiling in the file, were the only drag I could see. The game never told me what STAND was tied to.
answer.ending_fair_why: I reached the top, and the declassified card explained the key choice, the ceiling and the exposure number. The odd bit is that it says the hard ministry choice was at 52, while my notes put it around Y27-28. I couldn't square that.
answer.chase_next: The scandal ending at 85, where everything surfaces at once. I peaked at 28 exposure, so I want to play dirty and see the crash.
answer.play_again_why: I want to, but I'd need a break. A clean run to the top gave me few big surprises, and the late years felt flat and forced. A scandal run might be more fun later.

tone_breaks.line: The formula pays you twice the entry-grade minister's salary, and the formula was published, so nobody can say they were not told.
tone_breaks.note: It's a knowing, smug little aside. It's the only line that felt like the game nudging me, but it's mild.

answer.title_fit_why: The pay package ran through every year and the ending framed the whole thing around the salary formula. I didn't see anything called Confirmed & Substantive explained in my run.
